title: Three Afternoons and One Short Banner
subtitle: 节日庆典 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 节日庆典（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·节日与庆典）
meta: 主题语境：节日庆典（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·节日与庆典）　|　核心词汇：holiday　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 holiday 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 the organiser ① planned the holiday that no relative in the square would have described, and he said the planning was the whole of the afternoon. The ② holiday, meaning the break itself and not the banner, ran three afternoons and stayed undescribed in the book; a holiday, he said, is the only thing in a square that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ holiday in that square had the same short banner beside it, and the ④ holiday at the far fountain, meaning the parade they kept for the children to watch and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A holiday, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the organiser said the describing is the part that fills three afternoons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the holiday was the whole of the matter, meaning the reunion and not the break. The ⑥ holiday, meaning the reunion and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; holiday, he said, is either something you plan or the only word that means both a break and a reunion. He said the reunion is the part they remember.

By 1976 the ⑦ holiday had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the short banner. The ⑧ holiday of the whole thing, the organiser wrote in August, was one square and three afternoons of describing; holiday, he said, is either the parade at the far fountain or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ holiday I remember is the break described in the programme, which closed in 1978 and is still described as the quietest in the square. A ⑩ holiday, my mother said in 1980, is the only break that improves by being described; every holiday, she said, is a reunion that has agreed to look like a break. She said the reunion was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 假日；节日（指广场里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 假日；节日（指那个假期本身，与横幅相对）
C. 固定搭配：plan the holiday 安排这个假日
D. n. 假日；节日（指留给孩子们看的那一队那一个）
E. n. 节庆之事（抽象总称，指一处广场的假日之事）
F. n. 假日；节日（指节目册里写到、被记下的的那一个）
G. n. 团聚、欢庆（指一件事里人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 欢庆（抽象总称，指人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: planned the holiday that no relative in the square would have described
The holiday, meaning the break itself and not the banner
the holiday at the far fountain
the holiday was the whole of the matter
the holiday had become a line in a programme
The holiday of the whole thing
A holiday, my mother said in 1980

answers.why: plan the holiday 意为“安排这个假日”，1971 年那位筹办人把广场里没有一位亲戚肯描述的一个假日做了一遍。
holiday 意为“假日；节日”，指那个假期本身而不是横幅，它经过了三个下午而在簿子上没有被描述。
holiday 意为“假日；节日”，指广场里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一条窄窄的横幅。
holiday 意为“假日；节日”，指最远那座喷泉留给孩子们看的那一队那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
holiday 意为“团聚、欢庆”，指一件事里人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这次团聚就是那件事的全部。
holiday 意为“欢庆”，指人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个假期，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
holiday 意为“假日；节日”，指节目册里写到、被记下的的那一个，到 1976 年这一个成了节目册里的一行。
holiday 意为“节庆之事”，筹办人八月写道，整件事的假日之事是一处广场和三个下午的描述。
holiday 意为“假日；节日”，我记得的是节目册里描述过的那一个，1978 年过去了，至今仍被说成广场里最安静的一个。
holiday 为抽象总称，母亲 1980 年说，假日是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的假期。
